device.description: 12-bit 2 MSPS dual simultaneous-sampling 2x2 fully- / 2x3 pseudo-differential SAR ADC with 12-bit parallel interface, sequencer and programmable reference
device.note: ads7865.pdf (SBAS441C) p.3 recommended operating conditions (BVDD 2.7-3.6 V / 4.5-5.5 V), p.5 digital levels, p.6-7 pin configuration and terminal functions, p.7 Figure 1, p.8 timing requirements, p.17 configuration register (Tables 4-7), p.18 Figure 32, Table 8 (twos complement), p.19-20 sequencer register (Tables 9-13), p.21 reference DAC (Table 14), p.22 power-down and reset (Table 15)

registers.name: CONFIG
registers.note: p.17 Table 4 configuration register (default 000h; bit 3 don't care); written by a parallel write, no address

registers.name: SEQ
registers.note: p.19-20 Table 9 sequencer register (default 000h; SP read-only)

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: p.21 Table 14 reference DAC register (default 3FFh; bits 11-10 are 0)

registers.name: XFER
registers.note: internal state (not a datasheet register): DAC_WR=1 after a configuration write with R = 01, A = 001, SEQ_WR=1 after A = 100; the next write access carries that register's data (p.17 Table 7, p.20, p.21)

commands.name: Reference DAC value (second write after A = 001)
commands.note: p.21: DB[11:10] = 00, DB[9:0] the 10-bit DAC value (DB11:10 not checked)

commands.name: Sequencer register content (second write after A = 100)
commands.note: p.20 Table 9: DB[11:0] = S1 S0 SL1 SL0 CH1 CM1 CH2 CM2 CH3 CM3 SP1 SP0 (SP read-only)

commands.name: Device SW-reset (R = 01, A = 101)
commands.note: p.22: a configuration write with A[2:0] = 101 resets the device at the WR rising edge

commands.name: Write to reference DAC register with next access (A = 001)
commands.in: cc 01 d n e r x 001
commands.note: p.17 Table 7, p.21: the second write access carries the DAC value

commands.name: Write to sequencer register (A = 100)
commands.in: cc 01 d n e r x 100
commands.note: p.17 Table 7, p.20: the data on the second write access are the sequencer register content

commands.name: Read from reference DAC register with next access (A = 011)
commands.in: cc 01 d n e r x 011
commands.note: p.21: the next RD access provides the 10-bit DAC value on DB[9:0]

commands.name: Read from sequencer register (A = 110)
commands.in: cc 01 d n e r x 110

commands.name: Configuration update, deep power-down (R = 01, DP = 1)
commands.in: cc 01 1 n e r x aaa

commands.name: Configuration register update (R = 01)
commands.note: p.17 Tables 4-7: R[1:0] = 01 enables the update; other R values leave the register (write ignored)

pages: p.3 (ROC), p.5 (digital levels), p.6-7 (pins), p.7-8 (Figure 1, timing requirements: tCONV 13 tCLK, t10 20 ns), p.17 (configuration register), p.18 (Figure 32, Table 8), p.19-20 (sequencer), p.21 (reference DAC), p.22 (power-down, reset)
notModeled: analog inputs, the 2:1 fully-differential / 3:1 pseudo-differential multiplexer and the reference DAC / REFOUT (never driven): every conversion returns the 0 V differential code 000h
the two results per conversion (first RD: converter A, second RD: converter B) and read-once behavior (a further read gives 000h): every read returns the 0 V code 000h, which is indistinguishable
the sequencer (modes 0-2, LIFO result order, SP position) is not modeled

power-down: deep and nap power-down follow DP/N at the WR rising edge at once (the part: 2 us / 200 ns; wake-up 1 us / 6 clocks); a DAC/sequencer-read word with DP or N set does not power down in the model; auto-nap (AN) and reference power-down (RP) are stored only
the conversion is clocked by the external CLOCK (13 clocks from the first CLOCK rising edge after CONVST falls); the model uses 13 x 31.25 ns = 406.25 ns at fCLOCK = 32 MHz
bus float delay after RD rises is not specified (tDf 0)
vcc covers both BVDD ranges (2.7-3.6 V and 4.5-5.5 V) as one range
pin names: the minus sign of CHxx- is written '-'
variants: ADS7865 is the parallel-interface sibling of the ADS7863A (serial); separate spec.
